NKJV.1: Then all the congregation of the children of Israel set out on their journey from the Wilderness of Sin, according to the commandment of the LORD, and camped in Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.
NKJV.2: Therefore the people contended with Moses, and said, “Give us water, that we may drink.” So Moses said to them, “Why do you contend with me? Why do you tempt the LORD?”
NKJV.3: And the people thirsted there for water, and the people complained against Moses, and said, “Why is it you have brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?”
NKJV.4: So Moses cried out to the LORD, saying, “What shall I do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me!”
NKJV.5: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go on before the people, and take with you some of the elders of Israel. Also take in your hand your rod with which you struck the river, and go.
NKJV.6: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock in Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, that the people may drink.” And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
NKJV.7: So he called the name of the place Massah and Meribah, because of the contention of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
NKJV.8: Now Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
NKJV.9: And Moses said to Joshua, “Choose us some men and go out, fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in my hand.”
NKJV.10: So Joshua did as Moses said to him, and fought with Amalek. And Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
NKJV.11: And so it was, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed; and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
NKJV.12: But Moses’ hands became heavy; so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. And Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
NKJV.13: So Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
NKJV.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this for a memorial in the book and recount it in the hearing of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.”
NKJV.15: And Moses built an altar and called its name, The-LORD-Is-My-Banner;
NKJV.16: for he said, “Because the LORD has sworn: the LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.”

ESV.1: All the congregation of the people of Israel moved on from the wilderness of Sin by stages, according to the commandment of the LORD, and camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
ESV.2: Therefore the people quarreled with Moses and said, “Give us water to drink.” And Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the LORD?”
ESV.3: But the people thirsted there for water, and the people grumbled against Moses and said, “Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?”
ESV.4: So Moses cried to the LORD, “What shall I do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me.”
ESV.5: And the LORD said to Moses, “Pass on before the people, taking with you some of the elders of Israel, and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
ESV.6: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb, and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out of it, and the people will drink.” And Moses did so, in the sight of the elders of Israel.
ESV.7: And he called the name of the place Massah  and Meribah,  because of the quarreling of the people of Israel, and because they tested the LORD by saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
ESV.8: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.
ESV.9: So Moses said to Joshua, “Choose for us men, and go out and fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand.”
ESV.10: So Joshua did as Moses told him, and fought with Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
ESV.11: Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed, and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed.
ESV.12: But Moses' hands grew weary, so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it, while Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side. So his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
ESV.13: And Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his people with the sword.
ESV.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this as a memorial in a book and recite it in the ears of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
ESV.15: And Moses built an altar and called the name of it, The LORD Is My Banner,
ESV.16: saying, “A hand upon the throne  of the LORD! The LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.”

NASB.1: Then all the congregation of the sons of Israel journeyed by stages from the wilderness of Sin, according to the command of the LORD, and camped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.
NASB.2: Therefore the people quarreled with Moses and said, 'Give us water that we may drink.' And Moses said to them, 'Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the LORD?'
NASB.3: But the people thirsted there for water; and they grumbled against Moses and said, 'Why, now, have you brought us up from Egypt, to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?'
NASB.4: So Moses cried out to the LORD, saying, 'What shall I do to this people? A little more and they will stone me.'
NASB.5: Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Pass before the people and take with you some of the elders of Israel; and take in your hand your staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
NASB.6: 'Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, that the people may drink.' And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
NASB.7: He named the place Massah and Meribah because of the quarrel of the sons of Israel, and because they tested the LORD, saying, 'Is the LORD among us, or not?'
NASB.8: Then Amalek came and fought against Israel at Rephidim.
NASB.9: So Moses said to Joshua, 'Choose men for us and go out, fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will station myself on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand.'
NASB.10: Joshua did as Moses told him, and fought against Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
NASB.11: So it came about when Moses held his hand up, that Israel prevailed, and when he let his hand down, Amalek prevailed.
NASB.12: But Moses' hands were heavy. Then they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on one side and one on the other. Thus his hands were steady until the sun set.
NASB.13: So Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
NASB.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Write this in a book as a memorial and recite it to Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.'
NASB.15: Moses built an altar and named it The LORD is My Banner;
NASB.16: and he said, 'The LORD has sworn; the LORD will have war against Amalek from generation to generation.'

WEB.1: All the congregation of the children of Israel traveled from the wilderness of Sin, by their journeys, according to Yahweh’s commandment, and encamped in Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.
WEB.2: Therefore the people quarreled with Moses, and said, “Give us water to drink.” Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Yahweh?”
WEB.3: The people were thirsty for water there; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us, our children, and our livestock with thirst?”
WEB.4: Moses cried to Yahweh, saying, “What shall I do with these people? They are almost ready to stone me.”
WEB.5: Yahweh said to Moses, “Walk on before the people, and take the elders of Israel with you, and take the rod in your hand with which you struck the Nile, and go.
WEB.6: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock in Horeb. You shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, that the people may drink.” Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
WEB.7: He called the name of the place Massah,  and Meribah,  because the children of Israel quarreled, and because they tested Yahweh, saying, “Is Yahweh among us, or not?”
WEB.8: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
WEB.9: Moses said to Joshua, “Choose men for us, and go out, fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with God’s rod in my hand.”
WEB.10: So Joshua did as Moses had told him, and fought with Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
WEB.11: When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed. When he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
WEB.12: But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His hands were steady until sunset.
WEB.13: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
WEB.14: Yahweh said to Moses, “Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: that I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under the sky.”
WEB.15: Moses built an altar, and called its name Yahweh our Banner.
WEB.16: He said, “Yah has sworn: ‘Yahweh will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.’”

CSB17.1: The entire Israelite community left the Wilderness of Sin, moving from one place to the next according to the LORD’s command. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.2: So the people complained to Moses, “Give us water to drink.” “Why are you complaining to me?” Moses replied to them. “Why are you testing <sup>ⓝ</sup> the LORD?”
CSB17.3: But the people thirsted there for water and grumbled against Moses. They said, “Why did you ever bring us up from Egypt to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?” <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.4: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, “What should I do with these people? In a little while they will stone me!” <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.5: The LORD answered Moses, “Go on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take the staff you struck the Nile with in your hand and go.
CSB17.6: I am going to stand there in front of you on the rock at Horeb; when you hit the rock, water <sup>ⓒ</sup> will come out of it and the people will drink.” Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.
CSB17.7: He named the place Massah <sup>[1]</sup> and Meribah <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓓ</sup> because the Israelites complained, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
CSB17.8: At Rephidim, Amalek <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓔ</sup> came and fought against Israel.
CSB17.9: Moses said to Joshua, <sup>ⓕ</sup> “Select some men for us and go fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with God’s staff in my hand.”
CSB17.10: Joshua did as Moses had told him, and fought against Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
CSB17.11: While Moses held up his hand, <sup>[4]</sup> Israel prevailed, but whenever he put his hand <sup>[5]</sup> down, Amalek prevailed. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.12: When Moses’s hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat down on it. Then Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on one side and one on the other so that his hands remained steady until the sun went down.
CSB17.13: So Joshua defeated Amalek and his army <sup>[6]</sup> with the sword.
CSB17.14: The LORD then said to Moses, “Write this down on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua: I will completely blot out the memory of Amalek under heaven.” <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.15: And Moses built an altar <sup>ⓘ</sup> and named it, “The LORD Is My Banner.” <sup>[7]</sup>
CSB17.16: He said, “Indeed, my hand is lifted up toward <sup>[8]</sup> the LORD’s throne. The LORD will be at war with Amalek from generation to generation.”

AMP.1: Then all the congregation of the children of Israel moved on from the Wilderness of Sin by stages, according to the commandment of the LORD, and camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
AMP.2: Therefore the people quarreled with Moses and said, "Give us water so we may [have something to] drink." And Moses said to them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you tempt the LORD and try His patience?"
AMP.3: But the people were thirsty for water; and the people murmured against Moses and said, "Why did you bring us up from Egypt to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?"
AMP.4: So Moses cried out to the LORD for help, saying, "What shall I do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me."
AMP.5: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pass before the people and take with you some of the elders of Israel; and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
AMP.6: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb; there you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people may [have something to] drink." And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
AMP.7: He named the place [where this miracle occurred] Massah (test) and Meribah (contention) because of the quarreling of the sons of Israel, and because they tested the [patience of the] LORD, saying, "Is the LORD among us, or not?"
AMP.8: Then Amalek [and his people] came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.
AMP.9: So Moses said to Joshua, "Choose men for us and go out, fight against Amalek [and his people]. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand."
AMP.10: So Joshua did as Moses said, and fought with Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the hilltop.
AMP.11: Now when Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed, and when he lowered his hand [due to fatigue], Amalek prevailed.
AMP.12: But Moses' hands were heavy and he grew tired. So they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side and one on the other side; so it was that his hands were steady until the sun set.
AMP.13: So Joshua overwhelmed and defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
AMP.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write this in the book as a memorial and recite it to Joshua, that I will utterly wipe out the memory of Amalek [and his people] from under heaven."
AMP.15: And Moses built an altar and named it The LORD Is My Banner;
AMP.16: saying, "The LORD has sworn [an oath]; the LORD will have war against [the people of] Amalek from generation to generation."

NLT.1: At the LORD’s command, the whole community of Israel left the wilderness of Sin and moved from place to place. Eventually they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water there for the people to drink.
NLT.2: So once more the people complained against Moses. “Give us water to drink!” they demanded. “Quiet!” Moses replied. “Why are you complaining against me? And why are you testing the LORD?”
NLT.3: But tormented by thirst, they continued to argue with Moses. “Why did you bring us out of Egypt? Are you trying to kill us, our children, and our livestock with thirst?”
NLT.4: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, “What should I do with these people? They are ready to stone me!”
NLT.5: The LORD said to Moses, “Walk out in front of the people. Take your staff, the one you used when you struck the water of the Nile, and call some of the elders of Israel to join you.
NLT.6: I will stand before you on the rock at Mount Sinai. Strike the rock, and water will come gushing out. Then the people will be able to drink.” So Moses struck the rock as he was told, and water gushed out as the elders looked on.
NLT.7: Moses named the place Massah (which means “test”) and Meribah (which means “arguing”) because the people of Israel argued with Moses and tested the LORD by saying, “Is the LORD here with us or not?”
NLT.8: While the people of Israel were still at Rephidim, the warriors of Amalek attacked them.
NLT.9: Moses commanded Joshua, “Choose some men to go out and fight the army of Amalek for us. Tomorrow, I will stand at the top of the hill, holding the staff of God in my hand.”
NLT.10: So Joshua did what Moses had commanded and fought the army of Amalek. Meanwhile, Moses, Aaron, and Hur climbed to the top of a nearby hill.
NLT.11: As long as Moses held up the staff in his hand, the Israelites had the advantage. But whenever he dropped his hand, the Amalekites gained the advantage.
NLT.12: Moses’ arms soon became so tired he could no longer hold them up. So Aaron and Hur found a stone for him to sit on. Then they stood on each side of Moses, holding up his hands. So his hands held steady until sunset.
NLT.13: As a result, Joshua overwhelmed the army of Amalek in battle.
NLT.14: After the victory, the LORD instructed Moses, “Write this down on a scroll as a permanent reminder, and read it aloud to Joshua: I will erase the memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
NLT.15: Moses built an altar there and named it Yahweh-Nissi (which means “the LORD is my banner”).
NLT.16: He said, “They have raised their fist against the LORD’s throne, so now the LORD will be at war with Amalek generation after generation.”

The Amalekites Defeated
The Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.
NIV.9: Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hands.”
NIV.10: So Joshua fought the Amalekites as Moses had ordered, and Moses, Aaron and Hur went to the top of the hill.
NIV.11: As long as Moses held up his hands, the Israelites were winning, but whenever he lowered his hands, the Amalekites were winning.
NIV.12: When Moses’ hands grew tired, they took a stone and put it under him and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held his hands up—one on one side, one on the other—so that his hands remained steady till sunset.
NIV.13: So Joshua overcame the Amalekite army with the sword.
NIV.14: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Write this on a scroll as something to be remembered and make sure that Joshua hears it, because I will completely blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
NIV.15: Moses built an altar and called it The Lord is my Banner.
NIV.16: He said, “For hands were lifted up to the throne of the Lord. The Lord will be at war against the Amalekites from generation to generation.”

NRSVCE.1: From the wilderness of Sin the whole congregation of the Israelites journeyed by stages, as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
NRSVCE.2: The people quarreled with Moses, and said, “Give us water to drink.” Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the LORD?”
NRSVCE.3: But the people thirsted there for water; and the people complained against Moses and said, “Why did you bring us out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and livestock with thirst?”
NRSVCE.4: So Moses cried out to the LORD, “What shall I do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me.”
NRSVCE.5: The LORD said to Moses, “Go on ahead of the people, and take some of the elders of Israel with you; take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
NRSVCE.6: I will be standing there in front of you on the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people may drink.” Moses did so, in the sight of the elders of Israel.
NRSVCE.7: He called the place Massah and Meribah, because the Israelites quarreled and tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
NRSVCE.8: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.
NRSVCE.9: Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some men for us and go out, fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand.”
NRSVCE.10: So Joshua did as Moses told him, and fought with Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
NRSVCE.11: Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed.
NRSVCE.12: But Moses’ hands grew weary; so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side; so his hands were steady until the sun set.
NRSVCE.13: And Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the sword.
NRSVCE.14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this as a reminder in a book and recite it in the hearing of Joshua: I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.”
NRSVCE.15: And Moses built an altar and called it, The LORD is my banner.
NRSVCE.16: He said, “A hand upon the banner of the LORD! The LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.”

NET.1: The whole community of the Israelites traveled on their journey from the Desert of Sin according to the LORD’s instruction, and they pitched camp in Rephidim. Now there was no water for the people to drink.
NET.2: So the people contended with Moses, and they said, “Give us water to drink!” Moses said to them, “Why do you contend with me? Why do you test the LORD?”
NET.3: But the people were very thirsty there for water, and they murmured against Moses and said, “Why in the world did you bring us up out of Egypt — to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?”
NET.4: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, “What will I do with this people? — a little more and they will stone me!”
NET.5: The LORD said to Moses, “Go over before the people; take with you some of the elders of Israel and take in your hand your staff with which you struck the Nile and go.
NET.6: I will be standing before you there on the rock in Horeb, and you will strike the rock, and water will come out of it so that the people may drink.” And Moses did so in plain view of the elders of Israel.
NET.7: He called the name of the place Massah and Meribah, because of the contending of the Israelites and because of their testing the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
NET.8: Amalek came and attacked Israel in Rephidim.
NET.9: So Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out, fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand.”
NET.10: So Joshua fought against Amalek just as Moses had instructed him; and Moses and Aaron and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
NET.11: Whenever Moses would raise his hands, then Israel prevailed, but whenever he would rest his hands, then Amalek prevailed.
NET.12: When the hands of Moses became heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side and one on the other, and so his hands were steady until the sun went down.
NET.13: So Joshua destroyed Amalek and his army with the sword.
NET.14: The LORD said to Moses, “Write this as a memorial in the book, and rehearse it in Joshua’s hearing; for I will surely wipe out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.
NET.15: Moses built an altar, and he called it “The LORD is my Banner,”
NET.16: for he said, “For a hand was lifted up to the throne of the LORD — that the LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.”
